label: Sequence-initial c/3/x, plus the first fed-back copy step in length-3 sequences
explanation: Two disjoint components. (1) t=0 with input c, 3 or x: fires on every such step (precision 1.0) at a small, fixed magnitude (c ~0.12 of max, 3 ~0.06, x ~0.03). This is 79% of activations but only 61% of mass. (2) Length-3 sequences at t=4 (recall_idx 1, where the model feeds back its first output orig(0)): fires on ~39% of these steps but holds the largest activations (top examples 0.75-1.0 of max), and is strongest when the fed-back token is c or 3 (88% precision there, 33% otherwise). Weaker spillover: t=5 in L=3 sequences, and t=1 x after k. Never fires on the delimiter step, on recall_idx 0, or past t=7. The combined predicate gets dev F1 0.87 and mass recall 0.87. I could not find a clean rule for which non-c/3/x L=3 t=4 steps fire.
